why: Take 3 has the most life: she checks who can see before she asks, and "Walk, love. Don't run" protects the secret while lengthening the empty door. It needed a refusal to overcome and a clear reason. The call and his walk to her side stay true to the sheet and sources [96030c4c4a1a18523a3fdbbb, 46eefe8aeccc89bdf0676b8f]. One conflict: the writer's guard note says a mercenary talks bonuses, but the scene sheet says he says nothing about money. I followed the scene sheet.
changes: Added the missing Fixer-to-Inez exchange: she gives way too fast, and 'The Bureau's paid' explains why she obeys.
Cut 'You sound wrong', 'What have you heard?' and his protect-her reason, because he must not suspect and she must sound ordinary. He now refuses, from take 2, and comes because she asked.
Linked the reason to his choice: 'It can't wait. Please.' makes 'Then the door can wait' necessary and plainly says he is leaving.
Changed the last line to 'Let me keep you a while': tender to him, and to the player, her using his love to hold him off the door.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: It's time, Miss Nikolaou. The Bureau's paid. Call Okafor across now.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Now? With the terrace looking? Yes. All right.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Are you alone, love? Come across. I've something to tell you.

beats.speaker: Okafor
beats.line: Just me. I've this door till shift's end. Say it here.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Not down a telephone. It can't wait. Please.

beats.speaker: Okafor
beats.line: Then the door can wait. I'm leaving it now.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Walk, love. Don't run. Let me keep you a while.
